proxyServerInfo:
Specify your HTTP and HTTPS corporate proxy server settings below (optional).
To enable package downloads during cluster deployment in environments without direct internet access.
settingsAwsSecretInfo: Enter the access key to deploy the cluster to your AWS cloud provider account below. See the <0>official documentation</0> for instructions on creating an access key.
settingsGcpSecretInfo: Enter the service account content (in json or base64 format) to deploy the cluster to your Google Cloud provider account below. See the <0>official documentation</0> for instructions on creating an service account key.
settingsDoSecretInfo: Enter the API token to deploy the cluster to your DigitalOcean Cloud provider account below. See the <0>official documentation</0> for instructions on creating an access token.
settingsAzureSecretInfo: Enter the necessary details to deploy the cluster to your Azure Cloud provider account below. See the <0>official documentation</0> for instructions on creating an service principal.
settingsHetznerSecretInfo: Enter the API token to deploy the cluster to your Hetzner Cloud provider account below. See the <0>official documentation</0> for instructions on creating an access token.
settingsSshKeySecretInfo: Enter the contents of your private SSH key below to access the cluster servers via SSH. It is assumed that the corresponding public key has already been added to the servers.
settingsPasswordSecretInfo: Enter the SSH username and password below to access the cluster servers. It is assumed that the user account, such as root or one with sudo privileges, has already been created on the servers.
settingsConfidentialDataStore: All confidential data entered in these fields is stored in encrypted form.
expertModeInfo:
Activate Expert Mode to unlock advanced user interface options tailored for experience users.
This mode unlocks advanced settings for fine-tuning clusters, including options hidden in standard mode.
usersHelp: People who can sign in to pg_genie. Accounts are stored in the console for now; LDAP and single sign-on can be added later.
resetPasswordHelp: At least 8 characters. The user is signed out and uses this password next time.
confirmRemoveUser: Remove {{username}}? They will no longer be able to sign in.
rolesHelp: Groups map to the built-in policies: admin (everything), operator (clusters, Patroni, SQL read/write, logs) and viewer (read-only). Add attributes and your own policies in Access policies for anything finer, such as data scope per team.
accessPoliciesHelp: Who may do what, on which clusters, with which data, and when. Users get permissions only from policies that match their attributes (group, team, region, …); deny policies win over allow policies, and anything not allowed is refused. Data scope rules are enforced inside PostgreSQL with a dedicated role per scope, so they apply to every query, view and function.
allowHint: Allow: everyone this policy matches gets the permissions below, on the clusters below.
attributesAndHint: All attribute conditions must hold (AND); any of the listed values matches (OR). Users listed by name always match.
attributesHelp: Attributes describe a user (team = analytics, region = eu, clearance = pii …). Access policies decide permissions and data scope from them. Keys are lowercase.
builtinHint: Comes with pg_genie and matches the group attribute. You can change or disable it, but not delete it.
builtinNoDelete: Built-in policies can't be deleted - disable them instead
denyHint: Deny: the permissions below are refused for everyone this policy matches, whatever other policies allow. For SQL, a deny policy with a data scope hides that data instead of refusing SQL altogether.
hiddenColumnsHelp: schema.table.column, with * as a wildcard: *.*.email hides every column named email; public.customers.* hides the whole table's columns.
noSqlAccess: No SQL access on this cluster.
policyDataHint: Limits what SQL can see. Empty fields mean no limit. Patterns use * as a wildcard.
policyRulesHelp: How policies combine: a permission is granted when at least one enabled allow policy matches and no deny policy does. For SQL, the strongest level wins (admin > write > read), data scopes of matching allow policies are combined, hidden columns from all matching policies add up, and the most generous row and time limits apply. A user with any data scope or hidden column never runs as superuser.
policyWhenHint: Optional conditions. Leave empty to apply always and from anywhere.
policyWhereHint: Which clusters the permissions apply to. Empty = all clusters.
policyWhoHint: Users this policy applies to: everyone, users by name, or users whose attributes match.
tablesHelp: schema.table patterns, e.g. public.orders or sales.*
testAccessHint: See what a user may do - on a cluster and database, from an IP address, at a time - and which policies decide it.
